title: The Human Microbiome: Association and Causation
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
Humans live with vast communities of bacteria, archaea, fungi, and viruses. The term *microbiota* usually refers to the organisms in a particular habitat, whereas *microbiome* may refer to their collective genetic material and, in broader usage, the organisms and their environment. Definitions vary across research fields, so a careful reader first asks what was measured: species, genes, metabolites, or functions. A stool sample, for example, offers useful information about one kind of material but does not represent every region of the digestive tract or every microbial habitat in the body.

Gut microbes can transform dietary compounds that human enzymes do not process alone, compete with invading organisms, and interact with immune and metabolic pathways. These mechanisms make the microbiome biologically important. Yet importance does not mean that one universal “healthy microbiome” has been identified. Communities differ among body sites, people, diets, ages, environments, and times. Even diversity, often treated as automatically beneficial, must be interpreted in context: a single number cannot tell us which organisms are present, what they are doing, or whether a change caused disease.

Many studies compare microbial patterns in people with and without a condition. Such comparisons can reveal an association, but the condition may itself alter diet, medication, movement, or the intestinal environment. Those changes can then reshape the microbiota. A third factor may also influence both. To argue for causation, researchers combine longitudinal observation, controlled interventions, mechanistic experiments, replication, and attention to confounders. No single method solves every problem, but converging evidence can make one explanation more credible than its alternatives.

Clinical translation therefore requires narrower claims than popular headlines suggest. Microbiota-based treatments have evidence for particular indications, including products intended to prevent recurrent *Clostridioides difficile* infection after antibacterial treatment. They are not general cures for every condition associated with gut microbes, and transferring biological material can transmit harmful organisms. The central lesson is neither “microbes control everything” nor “correlations tell us nothing.” It is that an ecosystem becomes medically useful only when the population, intervention, outcome, mechanism, benefit, and risk are defined precisely.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Every healthy person possesses the same microbial species.

options.label: B
options.text: Microbiome findings become clinically meaningful through precise definitions and causal evidence.

options.label: C
options.text: Stool samples reveal every microbial habitat in the human body.

options.label: D
options.text: Associations between microbes and disease should always be ignored.

questions.answer: 正解：B。測定対象、因果証拠、対象集団・介入・結果・利益・危険を正確に定義する必要があります。Aは個人差、Cは試料限界、Dは関連の仮説形成価値を無視します。

questions.prompt: How does the passage distinguish microbiota from microbiome?

options.label: A
options.text: Microbiota usually means organisms in a habitat, while microbiome may mean their collective genes or, more broadly, the organisms and environment.

options.label: B
options.text: Microbiota means genes only, while microbiome always means a single species.

options.label: C
options.text: The two terms have one fixed definition in every research field.

options.label: D
options.text: Both terms refer only to viruses found in stool.

questions.answer: 正解：A。microbiotaは主に特定部位の微生物、microbiomeは集合的遺伝情報、広義には微生物と環境も指します。B～Dは定義と分野差を誤ります。

questions.prompt: The word “converging” in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to

options.label: A
options.text: independently pointing toward the same conclusion

options.label: B
options.text: deliberately hiding a negative result

options.label: C
options.text: measuring only one person once

options.label: D
options.text: replacing evidence with popularity

questions.answer: 正解：A。異なる方法が独立に同じ説明を支持する方向へ集まることです。B～Dは隠蔽、単一測定、人気への置換であり異なります。

questions.prompt: Why cannot a stool sample be treated as a complete picture of the digestive tract microbiota?

options.label: A
options.text: It samples discharged material at a time and may not represent communities on mucosal surfaces, in the small intestine, or in other habitats.

options.label: B
options.text: It directly measures every body site with equal accuracy.

options.label: C
options.text: It contains no useful microbial information at all.

options.label: D
options.text: Ease of collection guarantees complete biological representation.

questions.answer: 正解：A。便は採取時点の特定物質で、粘膜面や小腸など別部位を同精度で表しません。B・Dは代表性を過大評価し、Cは有用性まで否定します。

questions.prompt: Why does the passage reject microbial diversity alone as a universal health indicator?

options.label: A
options.text: The same diversity value can contain different organisms and functions, and its meaning varies by site and condition.

options.label: B
options.text: Diversity directly reveals which organism caused every disease.

options.label: C
options.text: Higher diversity is automatically beneficial in every context.

options.label: D
options.text: A diversity number includes complete causal and functional information.

questions.answer: 正解：A。同じ多様性値でも構成種・機能が異なり、部位や疾患で意味が変わります。B～Dは単一数値から因果や機能を読み過ぎています。

questions.prompt: Which statement best illustrates reverse causation?

options.label: A
options.text: Disease-related changes in diet or medication may alter the microbiota.

options.label: B
options.text: Microbial composition can never change over time.

options.label: C
options.text: An association automatically identifies a treatment target.

options.label: D
options.text: Controlled interventions are less informative than headlines.

questions.answer: 正解：A。病気が食事や投薬を変え、その結果微生物相が変わるという病気から微生物への経路です。B～Dは時間変化、因果検証、証拠階層を誤ります。

questions.prompt: Which research strategy best strengthens a causal claim about a microbiome effect?

options.label: A
options.text: Combine longitudinal observation, controlled intervention, mechanistic experiments, replication, and confounder analysis so their different strengths converge.

options.label: B
options.text: Rely on one cross-sectional comparison and ignore medication, diet, and other third factors.

options.label: C
options.text: Use a popular headline as a substitute for replication.

options.label: D
options.text: Assume time order and mechanism from association alone.

questions.answer: 正解：A。時間順序、操作後変化、作用経路、再現性、第三要因を別々に点検し、一方法の弱点を他で補います。B～Dは関連だけから因果を飛躍させます。

questions.prompt: What does the statement “neither microbes control everything nor correlations tell us nothing” mean?

options.label: A
options.text: Microbes should not be treated as universal causes, but associations can still generate hypotheses that require causal testing.

options.label: B
options.text: Every microbial association proves a universal cause.

options.label: C
options.text: Associations have no scientific value under any circumstances.

options.label: D
options.text: Mechanisms, interventions, and confounders are unnecessary.

questions.answer: 正解：A。微生物万能原因論と相関無価値論の両極を退け、関連を因果仮説の出発点として扱います。B～Dはいずれかの極端へ戻ります。

questions.prompt: What is missing from the claim that a bacterium found less often in patients will cure the disease if taken as a supplement?

options.label: A
options.text: It needs evidence on reverse causation and confounders, delivery and function in the relevant habitat, a defined clinical outcome, safety, mechanism, and a controlled trial in a specified population.

options.label: B
options.text: Nothing; lower abundance alone proves both cause and cure.

options.label: C
options.text: Only a larger headline, because mechanisms and trials are unnecessary.

options.label: D
options.text: Proof that all patients have identical microbiomes.

questions.answer: 正解：A。低頻度は関連にすぎず、逆因果・交絡、到達・機能、機構、対象集団、臨床結果、安全性、対照試験が必要です。B・Cは因果を飛躍させ、Dは不可能な同一性を要求します。
